checks.detail: 186 exact original files: 32 frozen prepared records, 144 input-directory files, seven existing candidate contact.inp decks, and three original adapter sources. Eight acquisition-complete markers are read/hash-bound only. No recursive formal-training, native response, sealed or test/OOD payload selection.

Friction fields.npz is an input-only graph despite its filename. Current snapshot uses original INPUT_ONLY_UNSOLVED/UNSOLVED_CANDIDATE records; rebar commits are COMMITTED_INPUT_ONLY. NPZ bytes are only streamed, never decoded, so this review is not an independent numeric zero-state verification.

All 32 NPZ/metadata pairs are checked against their frozen prepared records, rebar card members and original deck hashes are enforced, and friction existing contact.inp hashes must match input_identity. Candidate_00 keeps the historical rebar v3 receipt/source; other rebar candidates keep v4. Nine nonexistent friction decks remain missing and are not regenerated.

Package mode recomputes inventory and requires full equality with snapshot_manifest.json; the earlier independently reviewed comparison manifests retain their original SHA check. Source hashing compares dev/inode/size/mtime/ctime before and after. Every original file and all eight closure markers receive complete post-package SHA/CRC/length/stat comparison.

Expected archive contains 186 original payloads plus four metadata/helper files, 190 members total. Package mode uses exclusive ZIP creation, deterministic regular-file metadata, one-MiB streaming and complete per-member SHA/CRC/length readback, plus exact member-set/count checks.

Restore preflights every payload before making the destination root; root must be new with no symlink ancestors, relative members reject absolute/parent traversal, and files are created using xb. Embedded original absolute paths remain unchanged. The caller must use a fresh isolated recovery location with no concurrent mutation.

README requires first checking the whole-ZIP SHA from the external snapshot receipt. The restore helper itself trusts the internal manifest and verifies all 186 payloads; it does not implement an external receipt/SHA argument and does not independently stream all three helper/document members. Full 190-member CRC/SHA verification belongs to package receipt. No internal manifest is described here as an external trusted signature.

Both helpers use one-MiB opaque streams and no numerical libraries. The inventory parses one bounded prior manifest at a time. Package/restore checks observe RSS below 30 MiB after relevant phases; these are rejection checks, not preventive OS limits. This review does not establish future packaging/restoration peak RSS.

Recovery copies existing original bytes only. It does not release tests, solve, train or make path-bound locks portable. Missing-deck regeneration, relocated/new execution and dependency/environment changes require the separately documented new identity/freeze process.

nonblocking_findings.finding: The coverage extractor recognizes member/archive_member/relative_path/repo_path fields, not path-only publication records. Independent small-metadata inspection found five additional GitHub source references for the same three adapter hashes. All three adapter contents are already covered via other recognized records; the 16 input-graph and 96 rebar-path conclusions are unchanged.
nonblocking_findings.scope: prior_content_matches is a recognized-schema match list, not an exhaustive list of every possible published source reference. The README now documents this limitation; the original inventory is preserved unchanged.

package_provenance_cycle_avoided: This static_review.json is package-external and absent from the package script metadata/payload lists.
recovery_limitations: Externally authenticate the ZIP against the trusted snapshot receipt before using the helper; the helper does not establish this trust by itself.
Use a fresh isolated destination without symlink ancestors or concurrent filesystem mutation. Existing session runtimes must not be selected as recovery locations.
Restoration is not an all-or-nothing directory transaction: I/O failure can leave an incomplete newly created root; preserve it for diagnosis and use a different fresh root on retry.
No NPZ was decoded in this review; zero-future semantics derive from original records and the reviewed producer, not a new numeric contents check.
Peak RSS limits are observed rejection checks rather than OS-enforced hard memory caps. Actual package/restore receipts must supply their own measured peaks.
All four helper/metadata members are checked by package mode; default restore verifies payload identity and requires the separate external whole-ZIP SHA premise.
